issues.title: Default binding explanation not clear
issues.author: Razumain
issues.body:
Originally posted by @ralienpp

The text says:

> In this case, the `dataTbsHash` value is the hash of the exact data that is hashed and signed by the signature format in use.

It sounds like you hash it twice, i.e. `dataTbsHash = hash(data)` ("hash of the exact data"), and then again `sign(hash(dataTbshash), ...)` ("that is hashed and signed...).

comments.author: Razumain
comments.body:
Thanks for pointing this out. That was not the intention of the text.

I think the confusion is caused by being overly technical with explaining how signatures are created. Which should be obvious.

It could be simplified with:

> In this case, the `dataTbsHash` value is the hash of the exact data that is signed by the signature format in use.

I'm not sure if we need to say more than this. What do you think?

issues.title: Requirement levels
issues.author: Razumain
issues.body:
We should discuss whether the present requirement levels are well motivated.

The current document states that a certificate compliant with the profile:

- MUST never expire
- MUST not support revocation
- MUST include the signedDocumentBinding extension

However. All certificate parsing software will have to evaluate expiration, revocation and signedDocumentBinding individually, and not from the context of whether a certificate complies with this profile.

The current MUST requirements makes sense, but it is hard to be certain that there is no legitimate use case where you for example may want to set an explicit expiration date.

Perhaps we should change all or some of these to RECOMMENDED/SHOULD, but leave it to each implementer to choose what best suits their use-case.
